target.title: fix(browser): scope the aria-label stop fallback to the composer form (follow-up to #285)
target.body:
Follow-up to the post-merge review note on #285.

## Problem

The `button[aria-label*="stop" i]` fallback added in #285 matches document-wide, so any visible non-generation stop control (read-aloud, voice mode, dictation) keeps `isStopButtonVisible()` true. `pollAssistantCompletion()` only finalizes when that value goes false, so a completed browser response could stall until the response timeout.

## Fix

Scope the fallback to the composer form and exclude the known non-generation stop controls that legitimately render there: `form button[aria-label*="stop" i]:not([aria-label*="dictat" i]):not([aria-label*="voice" i]):not([aria-label*="read" i])`. The `data-testid` selectors stay primary; the fallback still covers testid drift for the real generation stop, which lives inside the composer form.

## Validation

`pnpm run typecheck`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, full browser suite (626 passing). The fake DOM in `thinking.test.ts` gained faithful descendant-combinator and `:not()` matching so the scoped selector is actually exercised; new regressions cover read-aloud/dictation/voice stops inside and outside the form.

## Real-behavior proof (redacted)

**Live CDP capture during an ACTIVE generation on a production GPT-5.6 conversation tab (2026-07-10 14:5x EDT):**

```json
{"generating":true,"testidStop":1,"oldSelectorMatches":1,"oldSelectorLabels":["Stop answering"],"newSelectorMatches":1,"newSelectorLabels":["Stop answering"],"pageWideStopLabels":["Stop answering"],"cf":{"hasAppShell":true,"hasChallengeScript":true,"bodyLen":59167,"titleIsChallenge":false},"visibleProgressBars":0}
```

The real generation stop control (`aria-label="Stop answering"`) lives inside the composer form on the live DOM: the scoped fallback matches it 1:1 with the old document-wide selector (`newSelectorMatches: 1`, same node), the `data-testid="stop-button"` primary is present, and form ancestry holds exactly as the selector assumes.

**Behavioral evidence from the fork running this change:** reviews completing after the deploy (09:04, 13:31, 14:14 EDT on 2026-07-10) all finalized normally, which requires stop-visibility to drop when generation ends; none stalled to the response timeout.

target.title: fix(browser): finalize assistant turns on positive completion proof (stop preamble/mid-stream capture)
target.body:
## Problem

With GPT-5.5 Pro (browser mode), oracle intermittently captures the model's **opening preamble** ("I'll review the diff…", ~150 bytes) as the *final* answer. Pro streams in phases:

`preamble → brief settle → reasoning + connector/tool calls (minutes) → real answer → completion`

`pollAssistantCompletion` finalized at the **first settle**: the `(!shortAnswer && stableEnough)` branch accepted "stop control absent + text stable" with no proof the turn was done, and #293's short-capture guard never engaged because a preamble is bucketed `longAnswer` (≥40 chars). Several finalize paths (poller, confirm re-poll, raw `return candidate`, `recoverAssistantResponse`) could each return a preamble.

## Fix: a positive terminal-completion gate

Replace the absence-of-streaming inference with one shared, positive-proof classifier (`classifyTurnTerminal`) used by the node poller, the finalize confirm step, the recovery path, and (mirrored) the in-page observer. A turn finalizes only on:

- **proofA** — the finished-action bar present for N debounced cycles **and** content stable for `minStableMs` (guards the transient-bar / first-tokens race).
- **proofB** — a generous continuous-quiet window with no active thinking (drift-safe fallback).

Any content change (fingerprint-based, not length-only, so an equal-length or shorter rewrite counts), a visible stop control, or active thinking resets the clocks — so a preamble is structurally held until the real answer streams. Implausibly short captures must be proven by the bar (fail-fast, never a 1-2 token stub). The finalize/recover paths refuse rather than return an unconfirmed capture.

`buildThinkingActivePredicateJs` (in `thinkingStatus.ts`) is a side-effect-free **activity** veto (stop control / animated loading-shimmer / aria-busy / active present-tense status label / live progress bar / right-side reasoning sidecar). It is deliberately **not** keyed on the mere presence of a reasoning container — the collapsed "Thought for Xs" summary persists on every finished turn and on reattach, which a presence-based veto would hang on.

Tunable via `ORACLE_BAR_CONFIRM_CYCLES` / `ORACLE_TERMINAL_QUIET_MS` / `ORACLE_TERMINAL_MIN_STABLE_MS`.

## Validation

Beyond the unit suite, I dogfooded this by running a GPT-5.5 Pro **review of this PR against the fork build** three times: each run held through the full ~10-20 min reasoning phase and captured the complete review on the first attempt (no preamble). Each round's review then surfaced real residual edge cases, which I fixed across the commits here.

`pnpm run typecheck`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and the browser test suite are green (added ~15 regression tests, incl. a settled-preamble→thinking→answer sequence, the transient-bar race, equal-length rewrite, and the "Thought for Xs" panel must-not-veto case).

## Known limitations (honest disclosure)

The self-review loop converged in quality but flagged residual, DOM-only limitations I did **not** fully close here (happy to in a follow-up, or guidance welcome):

- proofB is inherently *absence-based*; if the action-bar **and** thinking selectors both drift/localize, a quiet preamble could still be finalized after the window. The principled fix is a positive same-turn terminal marker or **network-lifecycle completion** (CDP `Network` on `/backend-api/conversation`).
- the per-cycle signals (text/stop/bar/thinking) are read via separate `Runtime.evaluate` calls (a small TOCTOU); collecting them atomically in one turn-scoped expression would be stronger.
- proofA currently bypasses *all* thinking; ideally only *weak* stale-panel evidence is bypassed while *strong* activity (stop/shimmer/progress/active-label) still vetoes it.

Net: a strict improvement over the current first-settle behavior, with the remaining edge cases documented.

## Review response (commit 5bcdc558)

ClawSweeper's P2 was real and is fixed: a completed summary rendered as `Reasoning Thought for 12s` passed the old `startsWith('thought for')` guard, then matched the active `reasoning` prefix, keeping `thinkingActive` true forever (proofB starved, finished answer times out when the bar path is unavailable). Reproduced with a failing regression before the fix.

Instead of special-casing the reported shape, the completed-summary rule is now uniform: short visible text containing `thought for ` (the length bound is what separates a collapsed summary from a live sidecar trace, and worded durations like "Thought for a moment" now count). The panel check judges only visible text so `data-testid="reasoning-..."` cannot taint it. The two sibling matchers that kept the strict prefix were synced too: `matchesThinkingStatusLabel` / the generated `isActiveThinkingStatus` (closing an unguarded capture path via `pollGeneratedImageOrTextAssistantResponse`, which returns snapshot text with no independent thinking re-check), and the image-only chrome regex in both its copies. Regression fixtures cover the status-label and sidecar paths: bare, heading-prefixed, worded, no-space-concatenated, and minute-second summaries, plus a live-trace-must-still-veto case and a real answer mentioning "thought for" staying an answer.

## Real-behavior proof (three GPT-5.5 Pro browser runs, redacted)

The three dogfood runs were driven by a review harness that polls the output file and the ChatGPT status while oracle (this branch's build) captures. Per-run ledger rows (local run ledger, verbatim except path prefixes):

```
{"ts":"2026-07-09T16:59:08-0400","pr":"1","exit":0,"outcome":"clean","secs":701, "attempts":0,"diff_lines":984}
{"ts":"2026-07-09T17:32:19-0400","pr":"1","exit":0,"outcome":"clean","secs":1134,"attempts":0,"diff_lines":1089}
{"ts":"2026-07-09T18:01:50-0400","pr":"1","exit":0,"outcome":"clean","secs":1270,"attempts":0,"diff_lines":1402}
```

Harness poll excerpts during the runs (the preamble-hold behavior under test):

```
[run 1, +5m and +11m, ChatGPT status: response streaming]
=== has $OUT been written yet? (with the OLD oracle this'd already be a ~150B preamble) ===
OUT still empty - oracle is still waiting for the real answer
[run 1, +11m42s] === FULL CAPTURED REVIEW (2132B) === ... VERDICT: FIX-FIRST

[run 2, +4m30s through +13m30s, status: response streaming]
=== OUT === (empty - still holding, good)
[run 2, +18m54s] DONE size 2525B (complete P0..P3 + VERDICT line)

[run 3, +19m30s, status: response streaming] OUT empty (holding)
[run 3, +21m10s] OUT: 4022B DONE (complete review, first attempt)
```

Each run: launch line `launching GPT-5.5 Pro Extended review (attempt 1, oracle timeout 30m)`, zero retries, no preamble capture, full Pn/VERDICT review on the first attempt. The three reviews' findings drove commits dd2efd52, 220d9b09, and 0fad06c4 (commit timestamps interleave with the run completions above).
